dialogue.Introduction: Arr! A new face on the beach. The name is the Pirate, and I've sailed every stretch of water between here and the Ginger Island shore.#$b#Don't worry, most of the treasure is in me stories. Most of it.$h
dialogue.Mon: Ahoy, @. Another fine day for hauling nets. The fish are biting, and so am I when me coffee goes cold.
dialogue.Tue: The tide's out and the sand's full of treasure. Mostly bottle caps, but a pirate takes what the sea gives.
dialogue.Wed: Me parrot has taught himself to say Hello Captain. He shouts it at the gulls. The gulls don't reply, the rude things.
dialogue.Thu: Up before the sun, scrubbing the deck. A sailor's life is mostly scrubbing, @, and I love every bucket of it.
dialogue.Fri: Got a fish sandwich from the Saloon, and the Tavernkeep threw in a free drink. Best day of the week, that.
dialogue.Sat: Saturday means the market's busy and the Merchant is shouting about prices. Keep your coin away from him, matey.
dialogue.Sun: A quiet Sunday on the beach. Good for mending sails and telling lies about the big one that got away.
dialogue.Mon2: Oh, @! Didn't hear ye come up the beach. I'm not much for company, but I'm not chasing ye off either.$u
dialogue.Tue2: The Dryad says the sea remembers every ship that sank on it. I hope it remembers the good ones too.$h
dialogue.Wed2: The Dye Trader has been bragging about his purple goods again. Stay clear, matey. A sailor can't trust a man in a rainbow coat.$a
dialogue.Sat2: Ye look like ye've been wrestling a crab, @. I've been there, and the crab always wins.$h
dialogue.Fri2: The Angler has been pestering me for tips on hooking big fish. Told him to try patience. Didn't work on me, but kids are different.$h
dialogue.Mon4: Ye're a fine sight on a morning like this, @. Me hook has been sitting heavy for days, and yer company lightens it.$h
dialogue.Tue4: Between you and me, I used to think the sea was the only friend a pirate needed. Then the Guide wandered into me cabin lost, and I found meself talking all day.$l
dialogue.Wed4: The parrot's getting old, @. I worry about him more than the storms. Is that daft?$s
dialogue.Thu4: I spent years on ships full of cutthroats and not one of them ever asked how me day was. Ye do. It's noticed.$h
dialogue.Fri4: Fancy a drink at the Saloon tonight? I'll buy, if the Tavernkeep doesn't remember me tab.$h
dialogue.Sat4: The Dryad told me the sea has a memory. I hope mine keeps good things.$u
dialogue.Sun4: Quiet days suit me, @. Quiet days with ye suit me even better.$l
dialogue.Tue6: Ye know the Painter has been sketching the sea all week? He made me look proper handsome. I told him he should paint the treasure instead.$h
dialogue.Sat6: I've been mending this old sail for three days. Turns out I'm better at breaking things. Want to help?$s
dialogue.Mon8: I never told the Nurse this, but when the storm took me old ship, I nearly gave up on the sea. Then I saw the light from this beach at dawn and thought, that's home.#$b#Turns out home had a farmer in it.$l
dialogue.Tue8: Me old crew were thieves and liars, @. The worst part? I missed them when they left. Now I miss the quiet we share, and that's the truth.$s
dialogue.Wed8: I've been writing down all the stories I tell ye. Every one has ye in it somewhere. Don't tell the Merchant, he'll want to sell them.$h
dialogue.Thu8: Ye asked me once why I came to the valley. I was tired of being the scariest man on any coast. Here folks just want a fish and a chat.$h
dialogue.Fri8: Let's sit and watch the sun go down over the water. No treasure, no map, no cutlass. Just you and me and the gulls.$l
dialogue.Sat8: The Clothier said I looked good in a waistcoat. I said I look good in everything. Then I wondered whether ye think the same. Do ye?$l
dialogue.Sun8: I look forward to Sundays now. They used to be for sleeping off the rum. Now they're for ye.$h
dialogue.Thu10: Every time ye smile at me like that, @, I forget what I was saying. It's a dangerous thing for a pirate.$l
dialogue.Sun10: I used to think a pirate needed nothing but a ship and a cutlass. Lately I think a pirate needs someone to share the sunset with.$l
dialogue.danceRejection: Arr, a dance? I'd tread on yer toes and sink the whole floor. Ask me again when the sea is a bit friendlier to me feet, @.$s
dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer on the coast is a delight, @. The waves are warm and the tourists fall in for a laugh. Mostly they're lovely.$h
dialogue.summer_Sat: Hot as a cannon fuse out here today. Let's wade into the shallows and forget the rest of the valley for a bit.$h
dialogue.winter_Fri8: The sea freezes a bit at the edges in winter, but I still come out to watch the ice. Gives me reason to bundle up with ye by the fire.$l
dialogue.winter_Sun4: Winter's quiet on the beach. I like it. And I like the quiet with ye even more, if I'm honest.$l
dialogue.spring_Mon: Spring means the Painter takes his easel to the coast again. He always leaves a bit of paint on the rocks. The sea likes it, I think.$h
dialogue.fall_Tue: Fall is the best season to read by the fire with a mug of cocoa. I'm working on a tale. It might have a farmer in it.$h
dialogue.fall_15: Fall brings the big storms, @. I've learned to batten down the hatches and invite company. I'd rather it be ye.$h
dialogue.spring_20: Spring tides wash up all sorts of things. Last week a bottle came in with a note saying meet me under the big rock. I laughed. I went anyway.$u

rainy: Rain on the beach and the sea's gone grey, @. Best day to stay in, sip cocoa, and mend the sails by the window.$h

marriage.Indoor_Day_0: Good morning, @. The kettle's on, and the sea is behaving itself today.
marriage.Indoor_Day_1: Ye look well rested. Did ye dream of treasure? I did, and it was ye.$l
marriage.Indoor_Day_2: Sit down, love, I'll fetch ye a mug of cocoa from the pantry.
marriage.Indoor_Day_3: The house feels bigger when ye're out in the fields. Come home soon.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_4: Hush, I'm reading the tide tables. The sea is calmer today, so we'll go fishing later.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_0: Rain on the roof, @. Perfect weather for a story by the fire.
marriage.Rainy_Day_1: Ye're dripping on the rug again. Come here, I'll dry ye off before ye catch a chill.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_2: The gutters are singing today. Let's sit by the window and watch the sea turn grey.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_3: I hate the rain for sailing, but I love it for the cuddling.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_4: The Painter came by dripping like a wet hat. He wanted to paint the storm. I said paint me instead, and he laughed.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_0: The lamp is low, @. Come sit with me before the day gets away from us.
marriage.Indoor_Night_1: I was writing a tale about a pirate who finally came home. It's starting to sound a lot like me.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_2: The house is quiet tonight. I like it quiet, when it's quiet with ye.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_3: Ye smell of pine and fresh air. Come to bed, love, and tell me about the farm.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_4: Do ye hear the waves? They sound like a lullaby. Sleep well, @.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_0: Rain pattering all night long. I'm glad to have ye to keep me warm, @.
marriage.Rainy_Night_1: Ye're shivering. Here, take the blanket. The sea is loud tonight, but I've got ye.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_2: I used to hate storms. Now I just like the sound of ye breathing beside me.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_3: Rain on the window and ye asleep on me shoulder. Best storm I've ever sailed through.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_4: Goodnight, @. Let the rain do the singing. I'll do the holding.$l
marriage.Outdoor_0: Let's walk the beach, @. The sand is cool and the gulls are gossiping.
marriage.Outdoor_1: Look at the sea, love. It's wide and endless, but I've found the one spot I want to be.
marriage.Outdoor_2: A fine walk, this. Watch that crab, he's a grumpy one.$h
marriage.Outdoor_3: I could walk this shore forever with ye. Mind the sea spray, it's a bit salty.$l
marriage.Outdoor_4: The tide's coming in. Let's stay a while longer and watch it roll.$h
marriage.Good_0: Ye always make me feel steady, @. Like a ship finding its harbour.$h
marriage.Good_1: I've been baking a fish pie. Don't tell the Merchant, he'll think I stole his recipe.$h
marriage.Good_2: Do ye want to hear what the Dryad said to me today? She said the sea remembers the good days.$h
marriage.Good_3: The mail came in today. The Guide sent a book on navigation. He says I should read it. I said I already know the stars.$h
marriage.Good_4: Ye look happy, @. That makes the whole house glow.$h
marriage.Good_5: Let's go to the Saloon tonight. The Tavernkeep has a new barrel, and I want to show ye off.$h
marriage.Good_6: The Nurse says I'm finally healthy. I told her that's the cocoa, and ye.$h
marriage.Good_7: The sunset is right over the water tonight. Come sit here, I saved a seat.$l
marriage.Good_8: The Party Girl wants us at her party. I told her we'd be dancing with the sea. She didn't get it.$h
marriage.Good_9: Every morning I wake up, I look at ye first and count me luck. I've got a lot of luck now.$l
marriage.Neutral_0: Morning, @. The fish aren't biting, but the coffee is passable.
marriage.Neutral_1: Did ye remember to feed the chickens? The Mechanic says the coop could use new gears.
marriage.Neutral_2: I've been mending nets all afternoon. It's a dull job, but the sea needs it done.
marriage.Neutral_3: The wind's shifting. We might have rain by supper, so mind yer boots.
marriage.Neutral_4: Ye left yer hat on the hook. I've hung it up for ye. Don't forget it next time.
marriage.Neutral_5: Just fixing the hinge on the door. The Carpenter's wood is too soft for it, but it will hold for now.
marriage.Neutral_6: The Merchant came round asking for fish. I told him to buy his own. He did not take it well.
marriage.Neutral_7: Ye smell of wheat and hay. Good work on the farm today?
marriage.Neutral_8: I'll be out in the boat this afternoon. Dinner is in the oven if ye're hungry.
marriage.Neutral_9: The sea is grey and so am I. It will pass, love.
marriage.Bad_0: Ye left the door open again, @. The gulls think it's an invitation.$a
marriage.Bad_1: The Tax Collector has been sniffing around, grumbling about fishing licences. I told him to swim out and ask the fish.$a
marriage.Bad_2: Mud on the kitchen floor again. I'm not cross, but I'd like to be cross for a minute.$a
marriage.Bad_3: The bucket is empty and the boat is leaking. I'm not in the mood for jokes today.$a
marriage.Bad_4: The Goblin Tinkerer blew a gear on the pier. Now me rope is knotted and I'm in a rage.$a
marriage.Bad_5: I'm not angry at ye. I'm angry at the seagull who stole me fish, and ye just happen to be standing there.$a
marriage.Bad_6: The clock has stopped again. The Steampunker says it's the gears. I say it's the sea air.$a
marriage.Bad_7: Don't start on the curtains again, @. I'm not in the mood for chatter.$a
marriage.Bad_8: Leave me to me nets for an hour, love. I'll come round when me temper is back.$s
marriage.Bad_9: I'm sorry, @, I'm short today. The tide is wrong and the day has gone sideways.$s
marriage.OneKid_0: Our little one has been asking for a pirate hat. I told them a pirate hat is earned, not bought.$h
marriage.OneKid_1: %kid1 and me spent the morning at the tide pools. They found a crab named Captain. Terrible name for a crab.$h
marriage.OneKid_2: Quiet now, %kid1 is asleep on the rug. Come sit with me and watch them snore.$l
marriage.OneKid_3: The little one wants to sail. I said not until they can tie a knot, and they tied one in ten seconds.$h
marriage.TwoKids_0: %kid1 and %kid2 are fighting over the last cookie again. I told them the sea will swallow it.$h
marriage.TwoKids_1: The children keep stealing me spyglass. %kid2 says it's for spotting treasure, and %kid1 says it's for spotting ye.$l
marriage.TwoKids_2: Quiet at last. %kid1 and %kid2 are dreaming of mermaids. I think I'm dreaming of ye.$l
marriage.TwoKids_3: These two are lucky to have ye, @. I'm lucky too, and I tell the sea so every morning.$h
marriage.NoBed_0: I've put the bed in the cabin for the cat, @. Don't ask. I'll sleep on the couch.$u
marriage.NoBed_1: The mattress has a hole the size of a cannonball. We'll sleep on the floor tonight. Like sailors.$h
marriage.NoBed_2: No bed, no problem. I've slept in worse on ships. Come here, the floor is warm.$l
marriage.NoBed_3: I'll fix the bed tomorrow. Tonight I'm stretched across the rug and happy as a seal.$h
marriage.patio_Elliott: Let's take the cocoa out to the patio, @. The sea looks gold tonight.$h
marriage.spouseRoom_Elliott: Our room is cozy tonight. I hung the sails up to dry. They look like the sea has painted them.
marriage.funLeave_Elliott: Off to the beach to meet the crabs, @. Don't wait up, I'll bring ye a shell.$h
marriage.funReturn_Elliott: Back from the sea! I've come home salty and happy. Give me a hug before I drip everywhere.$l
marriage.Outdoor_Elliott: The breeze is nice on the porch, @. Let's sit out here and watch the boats come in.
marriage.spring_Elliott: Spring tides are bringing in a lot of driftwood. Good for the fire, bad for the lawn, love.$h
marriage.summer_Elliott: Summer's here and the sea is warm. I'd happily swim all day if ye came along.$h
marriage.fall_Elliott: The autumn winds are picking up. We'd best batten the hatches and keep a hot drink in hand, @.
marriage.winter_Elliott: Winter is cold, but the fireplace is warm. Come snuggle up, love, the sea can't reach us here.$l

situations.eye: The Eye of Cthulhu is gone, @. Ye'd think a giant eyeball would be easy to spot from the beach. It's not.$u
situations.evilBoss: Something foul crawled out of the deep last night, and ye put it down. Those worms are no friend of a sailor.$a
situations.skeletron: The dungeon is open now and the Old Man is free. Skeletron is gone for good, I hope. The Clothier has been quiet about it, and that's a good thing.$h
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee's buzz is silenced. Honey on the beach is a fine thing, but I'd rather not bump into one with a stinger.$h
situations.hardmode: Hardmode has come, @. The Wall of Flesh fell and the Hallow is spreading. The sea has stranger looks now, and so do the things under it. Keep yer cutlass sharp.$u
situations.mechs: One of those metal machines is smashed to pieces. The Mechanic has been whistling since, and I'm glad. Machines in the sea are no friend to a sailor.$h
situations.plantera: Plantera is down and the jungle temple is open. The Dryad sends her thanks, and I'd love to hear the tales from the jungle sometime.$h
situations.golem: The Golem has crumbled. The stone idol was a mess, and I'm glad the Witch Doctor's people can rest easier. He hummed a song about it all morning.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is gone and the celestial pillars have appeared. They shine like strange lighthouses. A sailor would trade a whole ship for a map of those.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is defeated, @. Ye saved us all. I don't know how I'd sail again if ye hadn't gone. I'm thankful.$h
situations.goblins: A goblin army was sent packing last night. The Goblin Tinkerer shouted at them to go back to their tinkering, and they did.$h
situations.pirates: Pirates attacked the coast last night and I sent them packing. I know, it sounds odd coming from me. A pirate has no patience for another pirate's manners.$a
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion was pushed back to the ice. My boots are still cold, but at least the sea is calm and the valley is safe.$h
situations.martians: Martians came down from the sky. The Martian Madness is over. I've seen stranger things at sea, but none that scary.$u
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night. Strange waves crashed on the sand and the crabs had a fit. I stayed in with a rum and a good book.$s
situations.eclipse: A solar eclipse last night, @. The sea went dark for a moment. I held me breath and thought of ye. Silly, I know.$l
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party on the beach today. I'm told there's a keg, and a dance. I'm told I'm invited, and I'm not sure I've got the feet for it.$h

festivals.spring13: Egg Festival! I hid me best egg in a cove, and a gull ran off with it. Now I've got a rival in the seagulls, @.$h
festivals.spring24: The Flower Dance! If ye want to dance, I'll take ye for a spin, but don't blame me if ye end up in the sea.$h
festivals.summer11: The Luau! I brought a pot of fish stew for the community soup. It's full of treasure, if ye know where to look.$h
festivals.summer28: The Moonlight Jellies! They glow right off the beach tonight. Walk the shore with me, @. I'll keep ye safe from the tide.$l
festivals.fall16: Stardew Valley Fair! I entered the fishing contest and lost to a kid with a plastic rod. I'm still a bit sore about it.$s
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve! The Wizard turned me into a skeleton once in the maze, and I still haven't forgiven him. Stay close, @, I'm easily frightened.$u
festivals.winter8: The Festival of Ice! Cut through the ice and I'll catch the biggest fish of the lot. Or fall in trying. Either way, it's warm if ye're there.$h
festivals.winter25: Winter Star! I drew ye in the gift exchange, @. I'm sure ye'll love whatever I wrapped in a treasure map.$h
festivals.spring13_spouse: Egg Festival with me favourite person on the whole coast. We'll hunt the eggs together, and I'll let ye win.$l
festivals.spring24_spouse: Dancing with me spouse at the Flower Dance! I'll step on yer toes, I promise, but I'll sail ye round the floor.$h
festivals.summer11_spouse: Our Luau! I made the best soup I've ever made, and I did it for ye, @. Taste the treasure in it.$l
festivals.summer28_spouse: Walking the moonlit shore with me spouse. The jellies glow like lanterns, but ye outshine every one of them.$l
festivals.fall16_spouse: The Fair! Me spouse and me teamed up for the three-legged race. We won, and I didn't even fall in the sea.$h
festivals.fall27_spouse: Spirit's Eve with me spouse. I'll hold yer hand through the maze, and I won't scream once. Maybe.$u
festivals.winter8_spouse: Ice fishing with me spouse on a cold morning. Ye keep me hands warm and I keep ye company. A fine trade.$l
festivals.winter25_spouse: The Winter Star! Me spouse gave me a map to a treasure, and the treasure was ye. I'll cherish that always.$l

loved.text: A pearl! The sea herself must have sent this. Thank ye, @. I'll wear it proud on me hat.$h

liked.text: Starfish and shells! Ye have an eye for the sea's little treasures. Fine work, matey.$h

neutral.text: Hm. Some dry land junk. Thanks anyway, @, I'll find a use for it.

disliked.text: Ugh, a gel? Slimy things in me cabin? Keep them away, I beg ye.$a

hated.text: That's an insult to a sailor, @. Dynamite and a bunny, and a bucket of trash besides. Take it back before the Merchant sees.$a

help: Arr, bit of help here? Don't make me ask twice.
Ye there! Me cutlass is busy, lend a hand!
Someone come and bail me out of this!
thanks: Ye fought like a true sea dog, @. I owe ye a fish pie.$h
Ye saved me hide out there, @. The sea would have had me.$l
battle: Arr! Walk the plank, ye overgrown slime!
Yo ho! Blow me down, here I come!
No treasure for ye, monster! Keel haul time!
For the beach! Nobody sinks our shore!
courage.hurt: Got a hard knock from that thing. Nurse says rest, so I am resting, and cursing the whole while.$s

danger.boss: A great beast is loose and the sea is restless, @. Ye know I will not sit this one out.$h
danger.invasion: Pirates, goblins, whoever is out there, they will find a sailor waiting. Lace up yer boots, @, and bring a cutlass.$h
danger.pumpkinMoon: A pumpkin moon hangs over the beach, and the scarecrows are wandering. Arr, I will fight them to the last sprout.$h
danger.frostMoon: Frost moon! The ice is creeping up the shore and the snowmen have teeth. I will not let them freeze me out, @.$u
danger.eclipse: The sun has gone dark and things are crawling out of the shadows. Stay close, @. We will sail through it together.$u
danger.bloodMoon: Blood moon, and the waves are red as wine. I hate a bloody sea, but I will sail into it with ye at me side.$l

events.after: Careful on the rope out there, @. The tide is quick on the way back in.

steps.say: Arr! Ye caught me polishing me cutlass, @. Pardon the mess.$u
Most folk who wander up the beach trip on the rope and end up in the tide. Ye didn't. Good sea legs.$h
Hold this bucket for a moment, would ye? The gulls have been at me windows again.#$b#Mind me hands, they're sticky with fish oil.$a

steps.question: Would you like to hear a sea tale?

answers.reply: Ha! Then pull up a crate. Sea stories are the only ones I never run out of.$h
Fair enough. The sea keeps its tales to itself, I suppose.$s

steps.say: Take this for the trouble. A seashell from a pearl diver. Every sailor should carry one for luck.$h

events.after: Keep that bandage dry, @. And thank the Nurse for me. She'll pretend she didn't enjoy it.

steps.say: Ah, @! Don't be alarmed. I've just got a fish hook stuck in me thumb. I'm not a coward, I'm just bad at hooks.$s
Hold still, you great sea dog. Dry land folk have better sense than to fish with their thumbs.$a
A pirate afraid of a hook. The crew would laugh me into the sea.#$b#But ye didn't laugh, @. Ye sat down and waited with me. That's a rare thing.$s

steps.question: Do you want to help with the bandage?

answers.reply: Good. Hold the cloth steady and keep the Nurse from teasing me too much.$h

steps.say: Keep the thumb dry for a week, sailor. And stop pretending you're fine when you clearly aren't.$a
Yes, Nurse. Thank ye, Nurse. Thank ye, @. I owe ye a fish pie.$h

events.after: I'll be on the sand a while longer, @. The sun's been generous today.

steps.say: Ahoy, @! Ye found me secret spot. The tide is low, so the treasure is showing its face.$h
I dug up a treasure chest here last spring. It was full of barnacles and disappointment, but the map was real.$h
Care to help me look? I've got a shovel, a spade and very little patience.$u
Ah! Here. A cracked pot and a crab, but look, a coin inside! Gold, @. This is what dreams are made of.$h

steps.question: Do you believe in buried treasure?

answers.reply: Ha! Ye and me will get rich, or at least get sand in our boots.$h
Ha, the sand is the best treasure of all. Hard to lose, too.$h

steps.say: Keep that map, @. Mark where ye find yer own treasure. I'll be right here, watching the sea.$h

events.after: Still looking at the stars, @. Come back and look with me sometime.

steps.say: Oh, @. I didn't expect ye out so late. The stars are bright tonight, and I was counting them.$h
Ye know the old sailors' rule. Steer by the brightest star. I think I've been steering by ye lately.$l
I used to sail with men who laughed at love. I laughed too, until I met someone worth steering toward.$l

steps.question: Would you sail away with me one day?

answers.reply: Then it's a deal, @. The sea is wide, but I'd rather see it with ye.$l
Fair. I'll be here watching the stars. Not going anywhere.$s

steps.say: Then let's make a promise under the stars. No treasure, no cutlass. Just the two of us and the tide.$l

events.after: Still here on the sand, @. Same stars, same tide, and me still wanting to be near ye.$l

steps.say: Ye came down to the beach at night, @. I was hoping ye would. I've something to show ye, if ye promise not to laugh.$h
I found a sea chest in the cove. Locked, of course. I tried to open it with a harpoon, and well, it's still locked.$s
Inside was a note from an old sailor. It said the only real treasure is the one who waits on the shore.#$b#So, @, I've been waiting on this shore for ye.$l

steps.question: Will you be my true sailing partner?

answers.reply: Then take this golden coin as our first treasure. Keep it safe, my love.$l
Take all the time ye need. The tide will wait. It always does.$h

steps.say: Ha, look at me, weeping like a child. Happy tears, @. The sea sees them and says I'm finally soft.$h

events.after: Home at last, @. Let me get the kettle on, love.

steps.say: Home at last, @! I've been sailing the coast all week, and the first thing I wanted was yer face by the hearth.$l
Ye kept the lamp lit for me. That's the sweetest thing anyone has done on this whole coast.$h
I brought ye a shell from the far rock. It's not much, but it hums with the waves when ye hold it to yer ear.$h

answers.reply: Good. I'll put the kettle on and tell ye every tale I've got left.$l
Then to the Saloon! I'll buy the first round, and the Tavernkeep can gripe about it.$h

steps.say: Our home, @. Our waves, our valley. I'm the luckiest sailor who ever walked up from the beach.$l
